title: Game score: how it is built, mixed and what it must not do

structure.seam: the loop's last bar carries the tail into the first bar; export with a crossfaded tail or pre-roll, never a hard cut

menu.tempo: slow to medium, a steady pulse
menu.role_in_mix: full range, it is the only thing playing
menu.why: a menu is heard before and between play: calm, recognisable, never tiring

exploration.role_in_mix: sparse bed under the world's own sound
exploration.why: medium intensity that can be heard for a long time, and leaves room for footsteps, ambience and dialogue

puzzle.why: quiet, minimal music lowers the load while the player thinks; elements can phase in as the solution builds

stealth.role_in_mix: sparse, muted, leaves room for footsteps and cues
stealth.why: a sparse arrangement leaves the sounds the player must hear audible

tension.role_in_mix: pulse and a rising layer under effects
tension.why: a state between calm and combat so the step into combat is not a cliff

combat.role_in_mix: dense, ducks for dialogue and loud effects
combat.why: layers are added as intensity rises; the music must still sit under hit sounds

boss.role_in_mix: the loudest state, still inside the loudness range
boss.why: the peak of the game's own arc

victory.role_in_mix: a short resolved phrase, then back to calm
victory.why: a stinger or short cue that resolves, not a loop

defeat.why: a short cue that lets the player reset

mixing.stereo: wide and soft, positional effects keep the centre and the sides they need
techniques: a state-driven bus duck that follows dialogue and loud effects, with a longer release than attack
an EQ duck on the speech and effect band as well as the level duck
layers built as stems that share one tempo and bar grid
a limiter only on the final game bus, never on a loop stem that will be summed
measure integrated loudness over a long capture of real play, not over one loop

dos.text: Make a loop long enough to hide that it loops: a minute is the least, two minutes or more is better, or give it variants and small random variation.
Finish the loop so its end carries into its start: a crossfaded tail or pre-roll, a gentle fade at the join, never a hard cut.
Build vertical layers as stems on one tempo and bar grid so any mix of them is in time.
Move between states on a bar or a beat, with a stinger or a fill bridging when the key or tempo differs.
Enter an intense state quickly and leave it slowly, and hold a change until the new state has lasted a moment.
Write material for every state the game can be in (menu, exploration, tension, combat, victory, defeat); one loop cannot serve them all.
Leave the band and the level that dialogue, footsteps and cues need; thin the arrangement in the states where they matter (stealth, puzzle).
Fit a stinger to the current key and harmony, and let it wait for a beat or phrase end.
Level the music for the platform it ships on (console, mobile, headset), and measure over real play.

donts.text: Do not loop a short phrase for the length of a level: repetition fatigue sets in and the player mutes the music.
Do not export a loop with a click, an abrupt end or a gap at the join.
Do not rely on a flat 3 dB duck under a loud full orchestra: it was found not enough, so duck by EQ in the speech band too.
Do not play combat music in exploration or the reverse: the music tells the player the state.
Do not flip between states every second: calm that lasts two seconds is a reload, not calm.
Do not master a game cue to a film or streaming loudness: console is -24 LUFS, not -14, and the music has to fit under the effects.
Do not fill the midrange under footsteps, dialogue and the cues a player must hear.
Do not write hits tied to a cut or a timecode: the player decides when things happen.

provenance.structure.loop_min_s: one reviewer's rule of thumb: a minute is usually the bare minimum, two at least (gamedeveloper.com opinion piece); not a measurement
provenance.structure.transition_quantise: stingers and transitions fire on a beat or phrase end (Berklee Online, Audiokinetic); the choice of next_bar is a starting value
provenance.structure.enter_intense_state_s: starting value: the source says enter quickly and leave slowly but gives no figures
provenance.structure.stinger_fits_key: Berklee Online: a stinger should fit the current key and harmony
provenance.structure.seam: crossfade the end with the beginning, fade gently at the loop point (wayline.io loop guide)
provenance.states: starting values for energy, layers and tempo (no sourced figures were found); the family choices follow the descriptions of puzzle, stealth, exploration and combat music in the sources of knowledgebase/media/game-score-dos-and-donts.md section 5
provenance.mixing.music_bus_rel_to_dialogue_db: Unity audio-mixing tutorial: music about -30 to -20 dB, effects -10 to -5, dialogue -6 to -3 on its example mix; the difference is used here as a starting figure
provenance.mixing.duck_under_dialogue_db: starting value: the search found no standard duck depth; Audiokinetic's case study found 3 dB not enough for a loud orchestra
provenance.mixing.duck_flat_db_floor_for_loud_orche: Audiokinetic case study: 3 dB was clearly not enough, so a flat duck should start above it
provenance.mixing.duck_eq_band_hz: ProSoundWeb: the speech-intelligibility band is 2.5-5 kHz; practitioner range, sources disagree
provenance.mixing.duck_eq_cut_db: ProSoundWeb: reduce the music 2-4 dB in that band
provenance.mixing.lra_max_lu: Sony console guidance: a maximum loudness range of 20 LU (secondary report)
provenance.mixing.true_peak_db: Independent G.A.N.G. IESD mix reference levels: -1 dBTP
provenance.mixing.techniques: Audiokinetic (Wwise HDR and ducking) and the sources of the knowledge file; a practice list, not a standard
